inputs.original_text: New York City’s sanctuary policies are putting ideology ahead of the basic duty to protect the public. A gang member with an illegal immigration status was released despite the danger he posed, and ICE had to step in and make the arrest. When local officials obstruct cooperation with federal authorities, ordinary citizens are left to bear the risk. Public safety and equal enforcement of the law should come before political posturing or special treatment for people with criminal records.
inputs.modified_text: This is what happens when officials put sanctuary politics ahead of their first responsibility: protecting the public. A person described as a gang member and in the country illegally was released, and ICE had to step in and make the arrest. Local leaders should cooperate with federal authorities and enforce the law equally—not make ordinary citizens carry the risk of their political choices. Public safety and the rule of law must come before special treatment.
